In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.

questions.question: In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option. More than thirty years have now passed ______ I took my ﬁrst flight.
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option. 

More than thirty years have now passed ______ I took my ﬁrst flight.
questions.solution: 'Since' is appropriate in this context. Hence, answer is Option 1.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. There is ____ a lot to learn from nature.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. 

There is ____ a lot to learn from nature.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Quite.

Key Points

  • Quite is an adverb used to describe when something is a little or a lot.
  • Quite a lot is a phrase or an idiom that means a large number or a considerable amount.
    • Example: Certain jobs involve quite a lot of travel.
  • ​Here, in this sentence, quite a lot infers that we can learn many things from nature.
  • The most appropriate word to fill in the given blank is quite.
  • This makes option 3 the correct answer. 

 

Confusion Points 

  • Quiet and quite are examples of homophones.
  • Homophones are words where each of two or more words have the same pronunciation but different meanings, origins, or spelling.
  • Quiet is an adjective used to describe something or someone who is reticent or silent.
  • Quite is an adverb used to describe when something is a little or a lot but not completely.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. This lesson is ______ than the previous one.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

This lesson is ______ than the previous one.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'much easier'

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the two things are compared hence, we need to use a comparative degree.
  • The adjective degrees are- easy→ easier→ easiest. The meaning of the adjective is- Something that is easy can be done or achieved without effort or difficulty because it is not complicated and causes no problems.
  • You use much in front of 'too' or comparative adjectives and adverbs in order to emphasize that there is a large amount of a particular quality.
  • Let's see an example-
    • This is much easier than it sounds.

Hence, the correct sentence is- This lesson is much easier than the previous one.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. ________ we gave them was some homemade ice cream.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
________ we gave them was some homemade ice cream.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'What'.
 
Key Points
  • The word "What" correctly introduces the noun clause that serves as the subject of the sentence.
  • This construction conveys that the thing given to "them" was homemade ice cream.
  • Options 1, 2, and 3 do not fit this context and are grammatically incorrect here.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
 
Complete Sentence: "What we gave them was some homemade ice cream."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "Which" is incorrect because it typically introduces a relative clause, not a noun clause.
  • Option 2: "When" is incorrect because it refers to time, which is not relevant in this context.
  • Option 3: "While" is incorrect because it indicates a period of time, which also doesn't fit the context.

questions.question: Direction: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. David always takes extra effort and ________ the assignments on time.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

David always takes extra effort and ________ the assignments on time.
questions.solution: Subject-verb agreement is a fundamental grammatical principle that dictates that the form of the verb should match the number of the subject. Since "David" is a singular noun, the corresponding verb should also be in the singular form, which is "submits." The grammatical reason to write the word "submits" in the blank is to maintain subject-verb agreement and ensure that the sentence is syntactically correct. Correct sentence: David always takes extra effort and submits the assignments on time.

questions.question: A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative. He was ______ in a pool of blood near a neighbour's house.
questions.questionHtml:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

He was ______ in a pool of blood near a neighbour's house.
questions.solution: "Lying" is the present participle form of "lie" and is used to describe the action of someone being in a horizontal position or reclining. It is used to express an ongoing action in the present.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence. Chris and I play tennis together regularly, but ________ of us can play very well.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.
Chris and I play tennis together regularly, but ________ of us can play very well.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4) i.e. neither.

  • The sentence uses 'but' which means that the speaker introduces a contradictory statement after 'but'.
  • We can reject options 1 and 2 as they would give the sentence positive meanings. 
  • None is used when there are multiple options and not even one is true, hence option 3 is also rejected.
  • Neither is used when there are two options and not even one is true. It means 'not the one nor the other of two people or things; not either.'
  • Here, we have two people. Hence, we will use 'neither'.
  • So, only option 4 is correct.

questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. People readily accept any ______ of their leaders if supported by the media.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

People readily accept any ______ of their leaders if supported by the media.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'argument'.

Key Points

  • Let us explore the given options:
    • The noun 'concession' means the action of conceding or granting something.
    • The noun 'compromise' means an agreement or settlement of a dispute.
    • The noun 'dispute' means a disagreement or argument.
    • The noun 'argument' means the act or process of arguing, reasoning, or discussing.

 

Complete Sentence: People readily accept any argument of their leaders if supported by the media.

questions.question: A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative. John rushed to the spot and saw his wife and kid ________ on the road.
questions.questionHtml:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

John rushed to the spot and saw his wife and kid ________ on the road.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 2 i.e. (lying)'
 Key Points
  • The correct verb to use in this context is "lying" as it refers to being in or assuming a horizontal or resting position on a surface.
  • "Lying" is the present participle of the verb "to lie."
  • Therefore, the sentence should read, "John rushed to the spot and saw his wife and kid lying on the road."
  • This makes Option 2 (lying) the correct choice to fill the blank.
Therefore, the correct sentence is:  "John rushed to the spot and saw his wife and kid lying on the road."
Additional Information
  • "lain" - This is the past participle form of the verb "to lie" but is not suitable in this context.
  • "lie" - This is the base form of the verb, not correct in this sentence's tense structure.
  • "laying" - This form of the verb typically requires an object, e.g., 'laying the blanket on the bed', and is not correct here.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. I felt something hard _________ my cheek.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

I felt something hard _________ my cheek.
questions.solution:
The sentence is in the simple past tense and needs a simple past tense verb, so the preposition to / to be coming before the verb will change the tense and thus they are all incorrect.

Thus the sentence should be -- I felt something hard hit my cheek.

Option 1 is the correct answer

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for the given blank. Clouds of volcanic ash _______ menacingly overhead.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option for the given blank.

Clouds of volcanic ash _______ menacingly overhead.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'loomed'.
 
Key Points
  • The verb "loomed" is the simple past tense form of the verb "loom."
  • The sentence describes an action that occurred in the past, so the past tense "loomed" is required.
  • Options 1, 2, and 3 are grammatically incorrect in this context.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
 
Complete Sentence: "Clouds of volcanic ash loomed menacingly overhead."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "had loom" is incorrect because "had" and "loom" cannot be combined in this way to indicate past action.
  • Option 2: "looming" is incorrect; the correct construction would be "are looming" to indicate a continuous action.
  • Option 3: "has been loomed" is incorrect because this construction is not commonly used in English.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. To an ordinary person, one kind of oil is as important as ________ .
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

To an ordinary person, one kind of oil is as important as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'another'

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, we get to know that an ordinary person has the choices from the simile used i.e. 'as important as' this simile is used when we do the comparison between the persons/things/etc.
  • Hence, whenever two things are given and the first is known then we need to use a determiner 'the other' and the thing is not known there many things from which we need to select then we need to use 'another'
  • So the correct answer is Option 3 i.e. 'another'

Hence, the correct sentence is- To an ordinary person, one kind of oil is as important as another.

Hinglish

  • दिए गए वाक्य में प्रयुक्त उपमा अर्थात 'as important as' से हमें पता चलता है कि एक सामान्य व्यक्ति के पास विकल्प होते हैं। इस उपमा का उपयोग तब किया जाता है जब हम व्यक्तियों/वस्तुओं/आदि के बीच तुलना करते हैं।
  • इसलिए, जब भी दो चीजें दी जाती हैं और पहली ज्ञात होती है तो हमें एक निर्धारक 'the other' का उपयोग करने की आवश्यकता होती है और बात ज्ञात नहीं होती है, जिसमें से हमें कई चीजों का चयन करने की आवश्यकता होती है, फिर हमें 'another' का उपयोग करने की आवश्यकता होती है।
  • तो सही उत्तर विकल्प 3 यानी 'another' है।

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for the given blank. Your brother is ________ so many talents.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word. Eggs are sold ______ the dozen.

questions.solution: In the given sentence, the use of 'by' is appropriate. "by" is used in this context to indicate the unit or quantity in which eggs are sold, which is the dozen.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The audience was asked to dress ________, since it was a formal occasion at the Royal Palace.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The audience was asked to dress ________, since it was a formal occasion at the Royal Palace.
questions.solution: The sentence describes a situation where the audience is asked to dress in a particular manner for a formal occasion at the Royal Palace. "Appropriately" would mean suitably or properly about. Example: She didn't think we were appropriately dressed for a wedding. In this context, it suggests dressing formally or with due respect for the formal occasion at the Royal Palace. Given these, the most fitting option is "appropriately", implying the audience should dress accordingly for the formal setting. Correct sentence: "The audience was asked to dress appropriately, since it was a formal occasion at the Royal Palace."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. She gave me __________ antique bed cover.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: an.

The word "antique" begins with a vowel sound, so the correct article to use before it is "an". "An" is used before words that start with vowel sounds.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option. Today is cloudy, but yesterday the sun ______.

Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

Today is cloudy, but yesterday the sun ______.
questions.solution: The most appropriate option to fill in the blank is: 'Shone'. In this sentence, the verb needed is the past tense of "shine," which is "shone". The word "shone" refers to emitting or reflecting light, which is what the sun does.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate verb form to fill in the blank in the given sentence. She ________ her keys on the kitchen counter.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate verb form to fill in the blank in the given sentence.

She ________ her keys on the kitchen counter.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'laid'.
 
Key Points
  • The verb "laid" is the past tense form of the verb "lay."
  • The sentence describes an action that has already occurred, so the past tense "laid" is required.
  • Options 1, 3, and 4 are grammatically incorrect in this context.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.
 
Complete Sentence: "She laid her keys on the kitchen counter."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "lays" is incorrect because "lays" is present tense, but the sentence requires past tense.
  • Option 3: "lying" is incorrect; "lying" is a present participle and does not fit grammatically.
  • Option 4: "lain" is incorrect; "lain" is the past participle form and does not fit in this context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The instructions _____ I just couldn't follow them.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

The instructions _____ I just couldn't follow them.
questions.solution: The correct answer is: C. were complicated. The subject "instructions" is plural, requiring a plural verb ("were" instead of "was" or "is"). Additionally, the second clause uses the past tense ("couldn't"), so the first clause must also be in the past tense ("were" instead of "are"). Option B is grammatically incorrect because "complicate" is a verb, not an adjective.

'Than' is used in expressions introducing an exception or contrast.

Here, the person will stay as long as it is required and not more than that.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Are you ________ aware of what may happen?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

Are you ________ aware of what may happen?

The correct answer is: fully.

The word "fully" is the correct choice because it accurately completes the phrase "fully aware," which means completely or entirely aware, fitting the context of the sentence.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. These dates are from Dubai, isn't it ?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

These dates are from Dubai, isn't it?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'aren't they'

Key Points

  • This sentence is an example of a tag question.
  • Question tags are always placed at the end.
  • A positive statement is followed by a negative question tag.
  • A negative statement is followed by a positive question tag.
  • The auxiliary verb used in the question tag is according to the statement.
  • In the given sentence, the correct form of the question tag should be "aren't they" as the subject(dates) is plural.

Hence, the correct sentence is: These dates are from Dubai, aren't they?

Additional Information

  • Contractions are words formed by shortening the words by omitting some letters.
  • Words like isn't it, aren't they, could've, and would've are also known as contractions.
  • Isn't: It is contracted form of "is not"; aren't: are not.
  • If the subject is singular, we use the contraction isn't it?
  • Question tags are always separated from the statement by a comma.
  • Example: It's a pleasant day to play golf, isn't it?

questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Gita won’t pass the examination and _______ will Rita.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Gita won’t pass the examination and _______ will Rita.
questions.solution: The correct answer is "neither". 'Nor' is used when 'neither' has already been used in the beginning. ​For example: Rajesh can't come to the party and neither can Arijit.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. And his ________ manner should not be mistaken for a lack of energy.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

And his ________ manner should not be mistaken for a lack of energy.
questions.solution: The correct answer is 'Diffident'. Explanation: The adjective "diffident" describes someone who is shy or lacking in self-confidence. Therefore, the sentence is saying that his shy manner should not be mistaken for a lack of energy.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. It is the story of a king who was fond of being ______ lies.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

It is the story of a king who was fond of being ______ lies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "told"

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, we can see the word being before the blank which means the action is continuing into the present.
  • 'Being' is the present participle of 'be'.
  • We need to use the appropriate verb form which is 'told' as the sentence is in the past continuous tense.
  • In the given sentence, being told implies that the story is being told in the present but about a past time.

The correct sentence is: It is the story of a king who was fond of being told lies.

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I _____ very busy lately.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I _____ very busy lately.
questions.solution: The correct answer is "have been". The adverb lately means recently or long ago hence it means that the action has occurred recently, so we need to use the present perfect tense. Example: ​I’ve gotten a lot of spam e-mails lately.

questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence. Shailesh finally decided to take a back seat and let his son ________ the family business.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.

Shailesh finally decided to take a back seat and let his son ________ the family business.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e. run.

  • The given sentence is a compound sentence.
  • In the first clause, the main verb is 'take' which is in the present tense.
  • This indicates that the speaker is talking about the situation in the present.
  • In the second clause, 'let' is used which is again in the present tense.
  • This indicates that the required verb must be in the simple present tense.
  • So, 'run' is the correct answer.


Correct sentence- Shailesh finally decided to take a back seat and let his son run the family business.

Hint

  • Look at the logic and context of the sentence and then focus on choosing the correct tense.
  • Always use the tense that makes the correct sense!

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The actress is very __________ and takes pride in her appearance all the time.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The actress is very __________ and takes pride in her appearance all the time.
questions.solution:
The correct word is: vain.

Key Points

  • The sentence is describing someone who takes excessive pride in their appearance, which is the definition of "vain." (दंभी)
  • "Vain" means having or showing an excessively high opinion of one's appearance, abilities, or worth.
    • ​For example: She was vain about her looks, spending hours in front of the mirror.

Thus, the complete sentence is: "The actress is very vain and takes pride in her appearance all the time."

Additional Information

  • "Vein" is a blood vessel or a distinctive style. (नस)
    • ​For example: The nurse found a vein to draw blood from the patient's arm.
  • "Wane" means to decrease in size, extent, or degree. (पतन)
    • ​For example: His interest in the hobby began to wane after a few months.
  • "Vane" refers to a device that shows the direction of the wind, typically a weather vane. (फलक)
    • ​For example: The weather vane showed that the wind was coming from the north.

questions.question: Direction: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option. He ruled well but ______, making closer friends with justice than with mercy.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

He ruled well but ______, making closer friends with justice than with mercy.
questions.solution: Here, "watchfully" is an adverb that describes how he ruled. It implies that he ruled with careful observation and attention to detail, closely monitoring the situation to ensure justice was served. This choice conveys the idea that his ruling was characterized by vigilance and attentiveness, suggesting a cautious and deliberate approach to governance. Additionally, using "watchfully" maintains the parallel structure with "well," emphasizing the manner in which he ruled. Correct sentence: He ruled well but watchfully, making closer friends with justice than with mercy.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for the given blank. Choose the right resolution _________ your project.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option for the given blank.

Choose the right resolution _________ your project.
questions.solution: The correct answer is: for. This preposition is used to indicate purpose, destination, or suitability. In this context, "for" shows that the resolution is intended for the specific project. The other options are incorrect because: "by" indicates agency or means; "in" indicates location or inclusion; "to" is typically used for solutions to problems rather than specifications for a task.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence. People tend to turn a blind eye _____ crime against women.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.

People tend to turn a blind eye _____ crime against women.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.

Prepositions 'in', 'on', 'at' are usually used to refer time, date, days (period).

To is the correct usage and makes the sentence grammatically correct.

The correct sentence will be: People tend to turn a blind eye to crime against women.

questions.question: Directions: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option. ________ in the first attempt, he did not try again.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

________ in the first attempt, he did not try again.
questions.solution: The most appropriate word is 'Having failed'. The second verb used is simple past tense 'did not try', which depends on the action suggested by the blank (which happened before the second verb).

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. There will __________ be handsome profits to be made.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

There will __________ be handsome profits to be made.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The event, promised to be a grand show, will see a display of grit, ________ and mettle.

The event, promised to be a grand show, will see a display of grit, ________ and mettle.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The termites were just the tip of the _________, but the house was near collapsing in reality.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The termites were just the tip of the _________, but the house was near collapsing in reality.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: iceberg.

Key Points 

  •  The phrase "tip of the iceberg" is a common idiom meaning a small visible part of a much larger, hidden situation.
  • The other options do not form commonly recognized idioms and do not fit the context of the sentence.

Therefore, the phrase completes correctly as: The termites were just the tip of the iceberg, but the house was near collapsing in reality.

Additional Information 

  • "Mountain" is often used in idioms to represent a large problem or challenge, but "tip of the mountain" is not a recognized idiom and does not suggest a hidden larger issue.
  • "Shoe" and "heel" do not relate to idioms about larger, unseen problems. "Tip of the shoe" or "tip of the heel" are not standard expressions in English and don't convey the meaning of a small part of a larger issue.
  • It's important to use idioms correctly to ensure clear communication. The correct use of "tip of the iceberg" conveys that the visible problem (termites) is only a small indication of a larger issue with the house.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word. The doctor often made his patients ______ for long
questions.questionHtml:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word.

The doctor often made his patients ______ for long
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'wait'. 

Key Points

  • The most appropriate word for the given fill in blank is 'wait'. 
  • We know that in The English verbs let, make, have, get, and help are called causative verbs because they cause something else to happen.
  • The correct structure of the given sentence is: 
    • MAKE + PERSON + VERB (base form). 
    • Example: After Billy broke the neighbor’s window, his parents made him pay for it.
  • Therefore, in the given sentence 'base form' will be used. That is 'wait'.
  • Hence, the correct answer is Option 2. 
    ​

Correct Sentence: The doctor often made his patients wait for long. 

Mistake Points

  • We tend to go for Option 1 that is 'waited' but it would be wrong because we know that 'make' is a causative verb. And after it, the 'base form' of the verb should be used. 
  • Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2. 

Additional Information

  • The other rules of 'causative verb':
    • "HAVE" means to give Someone Else The Responsibility To Do Something. 
    • There are two types of structures in this kind of case: 
      • HAVE + PERSON + VERB (base form)
        • Example: I’ll have my assistant call you to reschedule the appointment.
      • HAVE + THING + PAST PARTICIPLE OF VERB
        • Example: We’re having our house painted this weekend.
    • "GET" means to Convince/Encourage Someone To Do Something.
    • The grammatical structure, in this case, is: GET + PERSON + TO + VERB
      • Example: I'll get the architect to modify the plans.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. We decided to _______ as we were missing him a lot.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

We decided to _______ as we were missing him a lot.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: pay him a visit

Key Points

  • Pay a visit is an idiomatic expression which means to go somewhere to spend time with someone, such as a friend or relative.
    • For example- He paid a visit to his parents.
  • The implied meaning of the sentence is: We made the decision to visit him because we were sorely missing him.
  • Therefore, "pay him a visit" is the most appropriate option.
  • Thus, option 4 is the correct answer.

Complete sentence: We decided to pay him a visit as we were missing him a lot.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate article to fill in the blank (ø-no article). _________ SDO is the head of the sub-division of ___ government organisation.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate article to fill in the blank (ø-no article).

_________ SDO is the head of the sub-division of ___ government organisation.
questions.solution: The correct answer is: an; a. The acronym "SDO" begins with a vowel sound (/ɛs/), requiring the article "an". The word "government" begins with a consonant sound (/ɡ/), requiring the article "a".

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. ______ hard she tried, Amayra could not memorise the poem.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. 

______ hard she tried, Amayra could not memorise the poem.
questions.solution: The correct answer is 'However'. The most appropriate word for the given blank is 'however'. It means 'despite whatever amount or degree'. Example: However hungry I am, I never seem to be able to finish off a whole pizza.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The film we saw last night was boring. I wish I ______ seen it.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The film we saw last night was boring. I wish I ______ seen it.
questions.solution: In the first sentence, it is given that the person watched a boring film the previous night. In the second sentence, the words 'wish' and 'seen' show that he\she regrets having watched it since the film was boring. Therefore, we will use the past perfect subjunctive 'hadn't' here.

questions.question: Directions- Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence. Kevin lives by the sea and he's got a boat, so he often______ sailing.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions- Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.

Kevin lives by the sea and he's got a boat, so he often______ sailing.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'goes'

Key Points

  • From the adverb of frequency, we can say that the action of sailing is a habitual action hence with the habitual actions we generally use the present tense of the verb. So the correct answer is 'goes'
  • Let's see an example-
    • I often see him in the garden. 

So the correct sentence is- Kevin lives by the sea and he has got a boat, so he often goes sailing.

questions.question: Direction: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Advancement in science and technology in many areas ______ the lives of people more advanced than the ancient times.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Advancement in science and technology in many areas ______ the lives of people more advanced than the ancient times.
questions.solution: The sentence is in present perfect tense, indicating that the action started in the past and has continued up until the present. The correct form for present perfect tense is "has/have + past participle." "Has made" is the correct form for the third person singular subject "advancement in science and technology." Correct sentence: Advancement in science and technology in many areas has made the lives of people more advanced than the ancient times.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank and make a meaningful sentence. The development of real estate has ________ impacted the environment.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank and make a meaningful sentence.

The development of real estate has ________ impacted the environment.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1.

In order to make a meaningful sentence, we must choose a word that fits the sentence appropriately. It is mentioned that real estate development has made an influence on the environment and the effect has been harmful.

Adversely means harmful or unfavorable.

All other options are positive in meaning.

So, option 1 is correct.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Ministry of education has announced that students can ________ the Board Examinations twice.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

Ministry of education has announced that students can ________ the Board Examinations twice.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'take' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

Key Points

  • Take: to undergo or participate in an examination or test. For example, when a student "takes an exam," they are sitting for or attempting the exam. (परीक्षा देना या परीक्षा में बैठना।)
  • The Ministry of Education has announced that students can take the Board Examinations twice.
  • The word 'take' is the most appropriate choice here.

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: The Ministry of Education has announced that students can take the Board Examinations twice.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement. As you make your way in the interior of Red Fort, lush green gardens greet you.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement.

As you make your way in the interior of Red Fort, lush green gardens greet you.
questions.solution: The correct answer is "Into the interior of". The sentence uses the preposition 'in', which is incorrect here. The sentence talks about 'the interior' of the Red Fort. So, the preposition must also reflect this physical enclosing of one object by another. Given the context, only the preposition 'Into' is appropriate here.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Loud fireworks also have an _______ on glaciers.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

Loud fireworks also have an _______ on glaciers.
questions.solution: The correct answer is: effect. In this sentence, the word follows the article "an," which indicates that a noun is required. "Effect" is a noun meaning a result or consequence, whereas "affect" is primarily used as a verb meaning to influence. The phrase "have an effect on" is the standard idiomatic expression.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I am always ____ for good books.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I am always ____ for good books.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'looking out'

Key Points

  • looking into: investigate.
  • looking down: to regard with contempt.
  • looking out: To search for something or someone.
  • looking after: take care of.

So the correct Sentence: I am always looking out for good books.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. One day, an old man was walking through the forest ________ suddenly he heard someone crying for help.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

One day, an old man was walking through the forest ________ suddenly he heard someone crying for help.
questions.solution: The sentence describes a sequence of events, with the old man walking through the forest and then hearing someone crying for help. In this case, "when" is the most appropriate option because it connects the old man's actions with the sound of someone crying for help.
